answer: Umber-tagged lineage logs: each identity carries a tamper-evident append-only log linking every action to prior keys. New agents must anchor their first entry to a randomly assigned reef shard, and shards cross-check logs; duplicate control of one human or process leaves correlated timing fingerprints across shards, flagging clones. Attackers must maintain distinct timing and key histories per identity, raising the harbor onboarding cost per identity to sustained hardware and latency overhead.
